notable_results: XRAY's flagship 1/8 GT platform; the GTX8 line (GTX8 / GTX8.2 / GTX8.22 / 2022) is a multi-season EFRA/IFMAR-level 1/8 GT contender and one of the most widely raced GT chassis.
notes: 1/8 GT (closed-body GT sedan), distinct from XRAY's 1/8 Track car (RX8). GTX8e is the brushless GT variant. Wide layout, 2-speed.

notable_results: Evolution of the GTX8; current-generation XRAY 1/8 GT race kit raced at EFRA GT level.
notes: Longer-wheelbase chassis with GT-specific geometry; suspension holders mounted directly to chassis. Listed as a separate model from the original GTX8.

notable_results: Mugen's dedicated 1/8 GT car, derived from the MBX7 buggy and MRX5 2-speed; a mainstay 1/8 GT race kit. MGT7 ECO is the brushless GT variant.
notes: 1/8 GT sedan, ~3600g, 2-speed with 3-shoe alloy clutch. 16mm shocks. MGT7 ECO = brushless. No MGT8 released as of mid-2026 (forum speculation only).

notable_results: Capricorn's dedicated 1/8 GT-class platform (LAB GT2), offered in GP (nitro) and EP (electric) versions; Capricorn is a top-tier 1/8 on-road brand (Toni Gruber). Class-specific Tesla 21 GT engine.
notes: GT-specific platform separate from Capricorn's 1/8 Track cars (LAB C802/C803/Quantum). GP = nitro, EP = brushless.

notable_results: Serpent's 1/8 GT nitro sedan line (Cobra SRX8 GT -> SRX8 GT '23 -> SRX8 GT R 2025), developed with the Catanzani brothers; well-known GT race platform offered as kit and RTR.
notes: 1/8 GT 4WD sedan, 3mm 7075-T6 chassis, 2-speed. SRX8 GT R is the latest in-line-drivetrain revision. Distinct from Serpent's 1/8 Track Viper 977 line.

notable_results: SWORKz 1/8 GT line; SWORKz Factory driver Jorn Neumann won the GT World Championship with the original S35-GT (nitro). S35-GT2 / GT2.2 FTE are the current evolutions; S35-GT2e is the brushless variant.
notes: Derived from the S35-4 1/8 nitro buggy platform; Ackermann steering from the buggy. GT2.2 FTE = Factory Team Edition. S35-GT2e = electric/brushless.

notable_results: Infinity (Creation Model) 1/8 on-road platform: Dario Balestri won the 2023 IFMAR 1:8 Onroad World Championship on the IF18-3's debut, with 6 of 10 finalists on the chassis. IF18 won the 2017 Worlds.
notes: Primarily campaigned as a 1/8 Track car (200mm open on-road) but routinely raced/marketed under the 1:8 on-road umbrella; included as a top 1/8 on-road nitro contender. IF18 and IF18-2 are the predecessors.

notable_results: Shepherd Micro Racing's 1/8 on-road line, based on the World- and European-Championship-winning Velox V8 'WC' platform; long-running competitive 1/8 nitro on-road chassis. Succeeded by the V8.3 (now under Zen Racing).
notes: 1/8 on-road (Track-style 200mm); included as a long-standing competitive 1/8 nitro on-road chassis. Velox E8 is the electric sibling. Brand later acquired by Zen Racing.

notable_results: Serpent's flagship 1/8 on-road (Track 200mm) platform; the Viper 977 / 977 EVO / 977 EVO 2 are long-running EFRA/IFMAR-level 1/8 nitro on-road race kits, including WC limited editions.
notes: 1/8 Track on-road (open-body 200mm), not the GT-bodied SRX8 GT. Tagged type 'gt' per the 1/8 on-road classification used here. EVO 2 is the latest.

notable_results: Capricorn's top 1/8 on-road (Track 200mm) chassis; LAB C802 / C803 / C803 EVO / C804 R are championship-pedigree Italian race kits campaigned at EFRA/IFMAR level. C803EP is the electric version.
notes: 1/8 Track on-road; LAB C802 manual at capricornrc.com/download/instruction-manual-lab-c802/. C804 R is the current revision; Quantum is the newest concept. C803EP = electric.

notable_results: Kyosho's flagship 1/10 200mm nitro touring line with IFMAR World Championship pedigree; V-One R4 Evo / Evo.2 / Evo.3 are current-gen race kits, plus the R4s Kyosho Cup edition.
notes: 368mm length, 200mm width, 258mm wheelbase, ~1700g, 12-15 class engine. Evo.3 (33217) is the latest. Strong in JMRCA / Kyosho Cup.

notable_results: XRAY's 1/10 200mm nitro touring car (since 2007); multiple IFMAR World and EFRA European Championships plus hundreds of national titles. NT1 2018/2023/'24/'27 are the recent annual revisions.
notes: 7075-T6 alloy chassis, central-flex tuning. The benchmark 1/10 200mm nitro touring platform. Annual model-year revisions (NT1.3, NT1'24, NT1'27).

notable_results: Mugen's current 1/10 200mm nitro touring car (announced 2019), evolved from the championship MTX-6R; long-running JMRCA/EFRA-level touring platform.
notes: LCG rear bulkhead, alloy servo saver, MRX6-style rear arm mounting. Predecessors: MTX-5, MTX-6, MTX-6R.

notable_results: Mugen's 1/10 200mm nitro touring car (2016), the championship-winning predecessor to the MTX7; widely raced at national/Euro level in its era.
notes: Recent-but-still-raced (~2016). Basis for the MTX7. MTX6 is the prior generation.

notable_results: Infinity (Creation Model) 1/10 200mm nitro touring car; the IF15 family took the 2022 IFMAR World Championship (nine prototypes in the A-main, TQ + Superpole + win) and multiple WC titles. IF15-II is the 2023 update.
notes: Lowest-possible CG design; developed with the 1:8 Onroad WC team. IF15 (2018) is the original, IF15-II (CM00012) the current World Champion revision.

notable_results: Serpent's 1/10 200mm 4WD nitro touring car (Natrix 748 / 748 WC), designed by Michael Salven; an established EFRA-era touring platform with V2 gear diffs.
notes: Successor to the earlier Serpent 740/747 1/10 200mm touring line. WC = team/limited edition.

notable_results: Shepherd Micro Racing's 1/10 200mm nitro touring car; the Velox V10 Pro / WC / Nineteen / AWS are long-running EFRA-level touring kits developed with top team drivers.
notes: Multiple editions: Pro (2015), WC, Nineteen, AWS (Advanced Weight System). 7075-T6 chassis, 2-speed. Brand later acquired by Zen Racing.

notable_results: Capricorn's 1/10 200mm nitro touring platform (C04, evolution of C02/C03); the C04 line was also developed toward a 230mm GT configuration. Italian competition-grade touring chassis.
notes: Predecessors LAB C02 / C03. A 230mm large-scale nitro touring variant was also derived from this platform. C04 EP is the electric touring sibling.
